questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my study destination based on that the destination were (i) within the European Union and (ii) english speaking.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to find the information upon arrival, and there were several introduction modules.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance in particular other than a lot of information by email about collection of student card etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find accommodation, and you had to be aware of scammers. In the end, I booked an Airbnb that was expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find an accommodation in advance and as close to TCD as possible. It is possible to rent a room in a student accommodation, but you have to rent for a year and hope that you can find another student to rent the rest of the period.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered in advance at home and everything was in order when I arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An e-mail was sent out to students who had to register for courses. You could get help from Academic Registry, which is a student service.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful. There were limited courses that I could take, so not a lot of choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find courses beforehand on the website of TCD, and make sure which courses you can participate in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could only take bachelor level courses. The level was easier at the host institution, and limited preparation for class was required. I chose modules where I had to write an essay as the exam method, which made it less important to attend all the lectures.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same style of teaching with a professor and smaller classes of approximately 20-30 students. The professors had prepared powerpoints and reading lists for each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I enrolled in Food Law, Intellectual Property Law, Commercial Law and Corporate Governance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend Food Law because of the professor and the importance of food law within the European Union. If you like EU law this is a great course.

questions.answer: The housing was so expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of activities were available for students such as social clubs, a gym and other athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A membership at the gym located on campus was cheap and you can go there in between classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I did hiking trips in the weekend, and also trips to the UK. I can recommend to rent a car and drive along the coastline or take the train to the bigger cities in Ireland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the local culture, and the local people is friendly and easy to talk to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to local students from your class or attend the social activities at campus. The local students are friendly, so just say hi and introduce you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to get used to random people wanting to talk to you etc. in the bus or at pubs.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The local pubs were so nice and cosy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation as close to the city center as possible, be social during the week and explore ireland in the weekends, and participate in the introduction week.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a student leap card (travel card) to use the bus and train system.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting local students, international students and other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was adjusting to living in another country and at a place with new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
